title: On‑Prem Packaging: commitment bands, SQ automation, and upgrade cadence experiment
creator: Ruth Chen
description: Background: Enterprise customers evaluating Private/VPC and on-prem options cite two friction points: (1) opaque license packaging resulting in long procurement cycles; (2) slow security questionnaire (SQ) turnaround that blocks pilots. Goal: run a 6‑week experiment to test 3 packaging templates + an SQ automation workflow to reduce time-to-contract and increase conversion from pilot to paid deployment. Scope: propose 3 license packaging templates (Commit Bands, Node Credits, and Flex Subscription), define 3 support tiers, design an upgrade cadence policy (LTS windows, emergency hotfix SLAs, optional deferred upgrade add-on), and build an SQ prefill + Q&A automation bundle for Sales/SEs. Deliverables: pricing sheet for each template, sales quoting calculator, SQ runbook and templated responses, pilot contract language, playbook for engineering to surface upgrade cadence options and opt-outs. Success metrics: decrease avg legal cycle from 42->21 days, increase POC->paid conversion by 15%, maintain >40% gross margin on dedicated deployments, reduce time to SQ complete to <7 days for top 10 standard questions.
pricing_models: Commit Bands (recommended for mid-enterprise): monthly vGPU-equivalent credits sold in bands (Small: 2-8 nodes, Medium: 9-32, Large: 33+). Base license fee = flat platform charge + per-band credit rate with 1.15x overage pricing. Includes optional burst pool add-on.

Node Credits (preferred for simple quoting): explicit node-equivalent seats priced by node-class (nv8, nv16, nv48). Good for customers with predictable infra planning. Offers simple renewal math and clear upgrade path between node classes.

Flex Subscription (appeals to SaaS/scale customers): subscription tier (Core/Pro/Enterprise) with committed throughput and per-token surcharge above commit. Includes upgrade credits that can be applied for 90 days to reach higher LTS releases.
Add-ons: SQ Pre-fill + QSA review credits, On-site/On-call Support, Extended-retention observability (30/90/365 days).
support_tiers: Standard: business hours (M-F 8-6 PST), ticketed support, 1 business day response for P1s, quarterly review. Included in all packages.
Priority: 24x7 monitoring, 2 hour P1 response SLA, named TAM, monthly ops cadence. Priced as percentage uplift on license (typically +18-28%).

Enterprise Elite: 24x7 with SRE-backed escalation, 1 hour P1 response, dedicated cluster ops engineering for blue/green upgrades and canary windows. Reserved capacity pools and guaranteed upgrade windows. Custom pricing.
upgrade_cadence_options: Managed Quarterly: default cadence. Rolling upgrades during scheduled maintenance windows. Customers may opt into full cadence or deferred LTS.
LTS-12: 12-month Long Term Support lane for customers requiring stability. Security fixes backported and delivered within 30 days; feature upgrades opt-in only. Premium fee applies.
Hotfix Lane: critical security hotfixes delivered within 48 hours. Requires support tier Priority or above and paid emergency maintenance allowance.
experiment_design: Cohorts: A) Sales-led pilots (closed deals with AE involvement) using Commit Bands + SQ bundle; B) Self-serve pilots (SMB/mid-market) using Node Credits with templated SQ answers.
Duration: 6 weeks pilot + 4 weeks observation. Launch with 8 pilot customers (4 in each cohort) selected by sales ops and solutions engineering.
Primary metrics: legal cycle days, POC->paid conversion, win-rate on renewal, gross margin per deployment. Secondary metrics: CSAT from SEs, time to provision, SQ completion time.
Data capture: canonical spreadsheet for quotes, tagged CRM records, and an experiment dashboard (console-analytics) instrumenting conversion funnel.
engineering_requests: Small API surface to allow quoting calculator to pull node-equivalent pricing and estimated throughput cost (ENG: estimate 3 sprint-days).
SQ automation hooks: endpoint for prefilled SQ payload and tracking tokens (ENG: 2 sprint-days and SE bandwidth to validate answers).

Documented upgrade guardrails in the runtime (canary window config, deferred-LTS flag) and a toggle in console to opt a deployment out of immediate upgrade windows (ENG: design spike in Cycle 2026-W07).
legal_sales_artifacts: Draft contract addendum (term sheet) outlining commit bands, overage mechanics, and upgrade deferral clause (consolidated doc in Drive).
Standardized SQ prefill deck (drive.google.com/link-FILLME) and a list of 25 prioritized SQ questions with canonical answers for first-touch wins.
Quoting calculator (sheet + UI spec) and sample SOW language for on-prem maintenance.

2026-02-27: Eng architecture sync — agreed to small API surface and a prefill endpoint for SQ automation. Eng capacity confirmed for spike in W07.
2026-03-03: Legal reviewed draft contract language; requested explicit overage smoothing clause and clarified termination rights. Action: update addendum.
2026-03-08: Selected 8 pilot accounts with Sales; SEs assigned. Set success targets per cohort and instrumentation owner (Analytics: Priya Rao).
2026-03-10: PM reviewed pricing worksheets and finalized playbook draft for pilot kickoff next week.
decisions: Favor Commit Bands as primary pitch for enterprise pilots — tradeoff: slightly more complex quoting in exchange for predictable revenue and higher margins.
Include SQ Pre-fill as a commercialized add-on (discounted during pilot) to measure lift in conversion time.
Offer LTS-12 as a paid add-on rather than the default to avoid upgrade lag across fleet; provides a clear revenue stream for stability work.
risks: Legal friction on overage definitions could reintroduce procurement delays — mitigations: explicit smoothing formula and example calculators in the SOW.
Engineering bandwidth to deliver toggleable upgrade opt-outs may slip — mitigation: scope minimum viable toggle and limit to Priority/Enterprise tiers initially.
SQ automation may not cover customer-specific questions; plan includes a rapid Q&A SLA and credits for QSA review.
